rationale: Adopt React Aria Components as the primary accessible primitive layer, with react-aria and react-stately as its lower-level hooks/state runtime. It has the broadest coverage in this batch: collections, tables, date/time, drag-and-drop, overlays, menus, forms and internationalization, all unstyled and Apache-2.0. The React 19 dialog spike opened with role=dialog, an accessible label and focus inside; the bundle was 277.23 KB / 88.22 KB gzip. The trade-offs are a 68 MB install with React and no npm provenance, so pin exact versions and record the gap. Base UI is adopted as the approved alternative: MIT, provenance-signed, React 17/18/19, about 30 MB installed, and a 257.79 KB / 82.46 KB gzip dialog spike with role=dialog, labelledby, describedby and focus inside. Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI and Ariakit are held, not rejected: they are viable for focused surfaces or existing codebases, but Radix is narrower and the unified package installs 76 packages, Headless UI has a narrower catalogue, Ark UI pins 69 @zag-js packages, and Ariakit is still 0.x. Styled systems such as Mantine, Chakra UI, MUI, Ant Design, HeroUI, Fluent UI and React Spectrum S2 are reference alternatives, not headless primitives.
scope: Library selection for React DOM UI primitives. Visual design, theming, application-specific accessibility testing and styled design systems are consumer obligations.
criteria: Permissive license across the full dependency tree
Accessible primitives with keyboard, focus management and ARIA semantics
Unstyled or minimally styled primitives; no required CSS-in-JS runtime
Actively maintained: a release within 12 months
No unfixed high or critical advisories
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Client-only rendering is acceptable; React Server Components are not required
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap

alternatives_considered.name: React Aria Components 1.22.1 + react-aria 3.53.1 + react-stately 3.51.0
alternatives_considered.reason: Broadest accessible coverage, Apache-2.0, active, React 18/19, unstyled and no CSS runtime. Dialog spike passed with role, label and focus. Costs: 68 MB install with React and no npm provenance.

alternatives_considered.name: Base UI 1.9.0
alternatives_considered.reason: MIT, provenance-signed, active, React 17/18/19, about 30 MB installed and a clean dialog spike. Broader than Radix but less comprehensive than React Aria for complex tables and date/time.

alternatives_considered.name: Radix UI 1.8.1
alternatives_considered.reason: Mature, active and provenance-signed with the smallest dialog bundle, but the unified package installs 76 packages and coverage of complex tables/date-time is narrower. Use individual @radix-ui/react-* packages for focused surfaces or existing Radix codebases.

alternatives_considered.name: Headless UI 2.2.10
alternatives_considered.reason: Clean MIT headless components and a good dialog spike, but a narrower catalogue and about 63 MB installed with React. Good for simple Tailwind overlays, not a broad foundation.

alternatives_considered.name: Ark UI 5.40.0
alternatives_considered.reason: Broad, active and provenance-signed, but 69 pinned @zag-js dependencies and about 44 MB installed. Good fallback if its state-machine API fits.

alternatives_considered.name: Ariakit 0.4.42
alternatives_considered.reason: Composable, provenance-signed and only about 18 MB installed, but still 0.x and narrower than React Aria or Base UI.

alternatives_considered.name: Mantine / Chakra UI / MUI / Ant Design / HeroUI / Fluent UI / React Spectrum S2
alternatives_considered.reason: Styled design systems, not headless primitives. They are outside this requirement's scope.

conditions: Pin react-aria-components 1.22.1, react-aria 3.53.1 and react-stately 3.51.0 exactly; pin @base-ui/react 1.9.0 if it is used.
Record the missing npm provenance for the React Aria packages and pin exact versions.
Use React Aria Components for complex widgets and react-aria hooks only when the component layer cannot express the primitive.
Do not mix React Aria and Base UI primitives in the same overlay, focus scope or form surface.
Do not add a CSS-in-JS runtime for these primitives; supply plain CSS, CSS modules or an existing styling layer.
Run an application-specific accessibility check with a screen reader and keyboard before release.
If Base UI is used, import from @base-ui/react and its component subpaths; do not use the deprecated @base-ui-components/react package.
If Radix is used for an existing surface, prefer individual @radix-ui/react-* packages rather than the unified radix-ui meta-package.
unknowns: The dialog spike covered one primitive; tables, date/time, drag-and-drop, combobox and screen-reader output were not exercised.
React 18 was not spiked; the peer ranges cover it, but the consuming application should verify React 18 if used.
React Aria does not publish npm provenance; the exact tarballs need pinning and review.
Install sizes include React 19 and vary with deduping and the consuming application's package manager.
Styled design systems were not reviewed in depth because they are outside the headless scope.
reversal_cost: Moderate: swapping the primitive layer means replacing component imports and re-testing focus, overlays and keyboard behaviour. Base UI is the cheapest alternative because it is already adopted.
review_triggers: A new high or critical advisory affects React Aria, Base UI, Radix, Headless UI, Ark UI or Ariakit.
A package stops releasing within 12 months or drops React 18/19.
The npm provenance or publish pipeline changes for the adopted packages.
The application needs a complex widget that React Aria supports poorly.
Base UI reaches a major release with materially better coverage or stability.
A styled design system becomes the preferred path and this requirement is re-scoped.
